description: acceptance/0 manifest — JSON Schema (draft 2020-12), version 0.1.0-draft. GENERATED FILE: produced by `tools/emit_schema.py`; do not hand-edit — regenerate it instead (a hand-edit will fail the drift gate on the next `gates/run_all.sh` run). NAMING: this file ships as 'schema/acceptance-0.1.0-draft.schema.json' while spec/core.md is UNSTABLE-UNTIL-FROZEN (spec/format.md 'Stability: acceptance/0 is UNSTABLE-UNTIL-FROZEN'); at freeze it is renamed 'acceptance-0.1.0.schema.json' (the '-draft' suffix dropped, no other change) and a new '-draft' cycle, if any, starts under the next minor version. SHAPE vs SEMANTICS: this schema is shape-normative only — table/field presence, field types, and closed-vocabulary membership. It is NOT semantics-normative: every constraint spanning more than one field (coherence rules, binding equalities, band reachability, hash recomputation, weight-conditioned requiredness, phrase floors, filesystem checks) is deliberately absent from the structural keywords below and is instead named in `x-semantic-only-rules`, and in the affected field's own `description`. On any disagreement between this schema and spec/core.md or spec/format.md, the spec prose and tools/check_acceptance.py win; this schema has a bug — regenerate it after fixing tools/emit_schema.py, never hand-edit the JSON. Generated from tools/acceptance_grammar.py and tools/check_acceptance.py's live registries — every closed vocabulary below is imported, never copied, so this file cannot drift from the validator that actually enforces it. See spec/format.md 'The schema artifact' for the normative statement of this split.

claim.description: [[claim]] entries. OPTIONAL as a key (a manifest may declare zero claims); when present, must be an array of tables ([[claim]] is a TOML array-of-tables).

items.description: [[claim]] — (spec clause, code item, evidence, assumptions). Open key set: fields not listed here (e.g. [[claim.assumes]], and the Reserved-hooks slots H1-H8 named in spec/format.md) are neither validated nor rejected by check_acceptance.py in this revision, so this schema asserts nothing about their shape either — see x-semantic-only-rules 'claim-open-extension-fields'.

band.description: The asserted evidence-species floor, A0..A4 (assurance-bands.md). 'A3.5' is a reserved band the validator warns on (tool not adopted). SEMANTIC: whether the band is actually REACHABLE by this claim's own passing evidence, and whether an oracle-bearing band's control-gate is satisfied, are both cross-field rules — see x-semantic-only-rules 'band-reachability' / 'band-control-gate'.

blocked_by.description: SEMANTIC: REQUIRED when status == 'blocked' (core.md §7.3, P4) — names what blocks the item; without it an escalation reads as a backlog entry.

bounds.description: This pattern checks only the leading 'bounded'/'unbounded' TOKEN. SEMANTIC: REQUIRED when grade is one of ['contract', 'probe'] (core.md §5), AND the token alone does not satisfy §5 — a free-text tail naming the actual limit is also required and is not pattern-checkable (x-semantic-only-rules 'bounds-free-text-tail-required').

clause.description: The spec clause id this claim is about.

clause_source.description: OPTIONAL in general. SEMANTIC: REQUIRED when weight == 'weighted' (core.md W2.3, transitional per §8.1); ['none', 'test-name'] are RESERVED to mean unweightable by design and refuse weight outright when present (x-semantic-only-rules 'clause-source-reserved-tokens-unweightable').

covered.description: N/M or 'N of M'. SEMANTIC: REQUIRED when item_kind == 'predicate'; N <= M is a cross-value check this pattern alone cannot express.

doc_ref.description: OPTIONAL. SEMANTIC (warning, not error): SHOULD be present when grade == 'inspection-argued' — never weight-eligible either way.

evidence.description: >=1 required when status is evidenced/partial; forbidden (must be empty/absent) when status is gap/parked/blocked (design rule 1 / core.md §7.3) — a cardinality rule conditioned on the sibling `status` field, semantic-only.

items.description: [[claim.evidence]] — an admissible evidence record (evidence-types.md). >=1 required when the enclosing claim's status is evidenced/partial; forbidden when gap/parked/blocked (design rule 1 / core.md §7.3) — a cross-field cardinality rule on the enclosing claim's `evidence` array, not expressible on this item schema alone.

alpha.description: RESERVED trust field (format.md design rule 3). Type is intentionally UNCONSTRAINED here — this node states no type at all: the live validator places no type requirement on this field, only the `calibration` companion above. It emitted `"type": "string"` until 2026-08-28, which REJECTED the calibrated numeric values the validator accepts; the description and the node now agree.

axioms.description: KIND_REGISTRY 'extra' field for kind(s) using it. Per-kind requiredness and exact tag (['list']) are semantic-only, conditioned on this record's own `kind` — see x-semantic-only-rules 'per-kind-extra-fields' and spec/evidence-types.md.

baseline.description: KIND_REGISTRY 'extra' field for kind(s) using it. Per-kind requiredness and exact tag (['str-nonempty']) are semantic-only, conditioned on this record's own `kind` — see x-semantic-only-rules 'per-kind-extra-fields' and spec/evidence-types.md.

bounds.description: KIND_REGISTRY 'extra' field for kind(s) using it. Per-kind requiredness and exact tag (['bounds-token']) are semantic-only, conditioned on this record's own `kind` — see x-semantic-only-rules 'per-kind-extra-fields' and spec/evidence-types.md.

calibration.description: OPTIONAL. SEMANTIC: REQUIRED (nonempty) whenever any of alpha/beta/lr is present (format.md design rule 3) — trust numbers without calibration are banned.

captured_at_commit.description: OPTIONAL (P3, evidence-types.md 'Control block'). 7-40 lowercase hex — a git object name, full or abbreviated, naming the commit at which this record's transcript was captured. DISCLOSURE ONLY: it is never a second validity key and this schema and the live validator both check it for shape alone — content identity is decided exclusively by `subject_hash`, above.

cases.description: KIND_REGISTRY 'extra' field for kind(s) using it. Per-kind requiredness and exact tag (['int-pos']) are semantic-only, conditioned on this record's own `kind` — see x-semantic-only-rules 'per-kind-extra-fields' and spec/evidence-types.md.

control.description: [claim.evidence.control] — OPTIONAL, family-agnostic (assurance-bands.md rule 6 / evidence-types.md 'Control block'). Open key set: the live validator does not reject extra keys here.

expectation.description: What this control was PREDICTED to show, declared before the run.

kind.description: mutation | ablation | planted-twin (assurance-bands.md rule 6). SEMANTIC: which kinds actually band-lift, and at which band, is a per-band whitelist — not expressible here (x-semantic-only-rules 'band-control-gate').

of_claim.description: SEMANTIC: must equal the `id` of the [[claim]] this evidence record is nested under (assurance-bands.md rule 6) — an equality binding, not a shape constraint. A value naming no claim anywhere in the file is a separate, additional error (check_dangling_of_claim).

corpus_size.description: KIND_REGISTRY 'extra' field for kind(s) using it. Per-kind requiredness and exact tag (['int-pos']) are semantic-only, conditioned on this record's own `kind` — see x-semantic-only-rules 'per-kind-extra-fields' and spec/evidence-types.md.

db_version.description: KIND_REGISTRY 'extra' field for kind(s) using it. Per-kind requiredness and exact tag (['str-nonempty']) are semantic-only, conditioned on this record's own `kind` — see x-semantic-only-rules 'per-kind-extra-fields' and spec/evidence-types.md.

duration.description: KIND_REGISTRY 'extra' field for kind(s) using it. Per-kind requiredness and exact tag (['str-nonempty']) are semantic-only, conditioned on this record's own `kind` — see x-semantic-only-rules 'per-kind-extra-fields' and spec/evidence-types.md.

epistemic_tier.description: OPTIONAL, closed core vocabulary T1..T5. SEMANTIC: where `method` names a token the shipped FV profile knows, the profile-pinned tier is a CEILING on `epistemic_tier` — a STRONGER declared tier is an error, a weaker-or-equal one is accepted (evidence-types.md CS-3, ADR-002) — a cross-field coherence rule, not independently checkable from this field's own enum membership.

family.description: bmc | kernel | smt-refinement | dynamic | mechanical | judgment. SEMANTIC: must equal the `family` KIND_REGISTRY[kind] pins — a cross-field consistency rule, not independently enforceable from `family`'s own enum membership alone (x-semantic-only-rules 'kind-family-consistency').

generator.description: KIND_REGISTRY 'extra' field for kind(s) using it. Per-kind requiredness and exact tag (['str-nonempty']) are semantic-only, conditioned on this record's own `kind` — see x-semantic-only-rules 'per-kind-extra-fields' and spec/evidence-types.md.

kind.description: The evidence-kind registry (evidence-types.md). Unlike [subject].kind, an unknown token here is a hard `invalid`, not `indeterminate` — this enum is genuinely closed in the live validator.

mutants_caught.description: OPTIONAL. SEMANTIC: >= 0, and additionally >= 1 whenever this record's own `result` == 'pass' (assurance-bands.md rule 6) — a cross-field floor, not independently expressible as this field's own `minimum`.

record.description: Pointer to the raw run record. SEMANTIC: must resolve to an existing file under `--strict` (or [subject].record_root, if set) — a filesystem check, not a shape constraint.

record_hash.description: The evidence-record-domain M11 hash of the `record` file. SEMANTIC: REQUIRED on a WEIGHTED claim's evidence when not illustrative (evidence-types.md P9); when present, the validator recomputes it from `record`'s actual bytes and a mismatch is always an error — recomputation and the weighted-requiredness are both semantic, not shape.

ref.description: The harness/theorem/test id — the checkable name.

result.description: pass | fail | unsupported (design rule 5: recorded as-is, never adjudicated).

reviewer.description: KIND_REGISTRY 'extra' field for kind(s) using it. Per-kind requiredness and exact tag (['str-nonempty']) are semantic-only, conditioned on this record's own `kind` — see x-semantic-only-rules 'per-kind-extra-fields' and spec/evidence-types.md.

semantics.description: KIND_REGISTRY 'extra' field for kind(s) using it. Per-kind requiredness and exact tag (['str-any', 'str-nonempty']) are semantic-only, conditioned on this record's own `kind` — see x-semantic-only-rules 'per-kind-extra-fields' and spec/evidence-types.md.

subject_hash.description: OPTIONAL. SEMANTIC: when present, must equal [subject].subject_hash exactly (design rule 4a) — an equality binding, not a shape constraint.

tool.description: Tool identity AT BUILD GRANULARITY (commit, not version).

grade.description: OPTIONAL structurally. SEMANTIC: REQUIRED when weight == 'weighted' (core.md W2); ['inspection-argued', 'ungraded', 'unspecified'] can never carry weight even when present (x-semantic-only-rules 'grade-required-on-weighted').

id.description: Stable, unique within the file, never reused (format.md design rule 6). SEMANTIC: file-wide uniqueness is a cross-claim rule, not a per-field pattern.

item.description: The code item the claim attaches to.

item_kind.description: OPTIONAL, defaults to 'item' (core.md §7.2). SEMANTIC: 'predicate' additionally requires `over` and a valid `covered` fraction with numerator <= denominator — a cross-field requirement, not expressible on this field alone.

over.description: SEMANTIC: REQUIRED when item_kind == 'predicate' — what the predicate ranges over.

scope_ref.description: A locator: a section marker, an anchor, a document path, or `[spec].axis`. SEMANTIC: REQUIRED when grade == 'out-of-scope' (core.md §1/§7.1); this pattern checks locator SHAPE only — that the cited location really says out-of-scope is reviewer work.

self_verify.description: [claim.self_verify] — the consumer-side recipe (core.md §3), distinct from evidence. CLOSED key set: check_acceptance.py errors on any key outside ['command', 'expect', 'expect_stream', 'positive_control', 'precondition', 'watched_fail'] (no legacy producers to tolerate typos from) — the other of exactly two tables in the format where `additionalProperties: false` is genuine validator behaviour, not a schema-author's guess.

command.description: The consumer-side recipe. SEMANTIC: REQUIRED (nonempty) whenever this claim's `grade` is one of ['contract', 'mechanical', 'not-covered', 'probe', 'test-only'] (core.md §1/§3).

expect.description: SEMANTIC: REQUIRED (nonempty) whenever `command` is present — 'what green means' has to be written (core.md §3 rule 2).

expect_stream.description: OPTIONAL, defaults to 'stdout' (core.md §8.2): which stream `--execute` matches `expect` against.

positive_control.description: SEMANTIC: REQUIRED (nonempty, phrase floor) when grade == 'not-covered' (core.md §4) — a grep zero is a claim about the pattern, not the code.

watched_fail.description: [claim.self_verify.watched_fail] — a structured witness that the recipe CAN report the claim false (core.md §4.1). CLOSED key set: check_acceptance.py errors on any key outside {of_command, perturbed, observed, date} — this table is one of exactly two in the whole format where `additionalProperties: false` reflects genuine, unconditional validator behaviour.

of_command.description: SEMANTIC: must equal this claim's own self_verify.command, whitespace-normalized — an equality binding across sibling tables, not a shape constraint (core.md §4.1).

perturbed.description: SEMANTIC: must be a PHRASE (>=2 word tokens after stripping a trailing date annotation) — a single token is not a statement (core.md §4.1).

statement.description: What is being claimed, in prose.

status.description: evidenced | partial | gap | parked | blocked. SEMANTIC: must COHERE with `grade` (core.md §7.1) and gates the `evidence` array's required cardinality (design rule 1 / §7.3) — neither is expressible from `status`'s own enum membership alone.

weight.description: OPTIONAL, defaults to unweighted (core.md W1). 'weighted' switches on the whole anti-overclaim machinery this schema marks SEMANTIC throughout this claim's fields.

claims_total.description: SEMANTIC: must equal the number of [[claim]] entries actually present — a cross-field count, not a type constraint (x-semantic-only-rules 'claims-total-must-match-claim-count').

clauses_total.description: Total clause count in spec@version. SEMANTIC floor: must be >= 1 (enforced by the validator; not encoded as `minimum` here to keep this schema's own numeric floors confined to fields the validator checks unconditionally — see x-semantic-only-rules).

denominator.description: OPTIONAL, EXPERIMENTAL (CLAIM-CLASSES-AWAITING-WEIGHT.md C1): complete | slice. Validated for shape only even by the live validator.

slice_note.description: SEMANTIC: REQUIRED, nonempty, when denominator == 'slice' — a conditional requirement, not encoded structurally here.

generated_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp; shape only, not parsed as a date by the validator.

generated_by.description: Generator id + version, or the literal 'hand-authored'.

id.description: The format id. Exact string; a breaking change bumps the integer (spec/format.md 'Stability').

illustrative.description: Defaults to false. true = a teaching example, not a certificate (core.md §0.6, CS-21/22) — several semantic rules below are not enforced against an illustrative manifest.

shape.description: single-file vs bundle (spec/format.md '`shape`'). SEMANTIC: 'bundle' makes the WHOLE manifest `indeterminate`, not just this field, until bundle validation ships — not expressible as a shape constraint (x-semantic-only-rules 'shape-bundle-indeterminate').

spec_id.description: Which contract this manifest is written against (core.md §0.6).

spec_sha.description: The spec commit/tag this manifest targets.

validator_sha.description: The validator commit that checked this manifest.

axis.description: OPTIONAL structurally. SEMANTIC: REQUIRED once ANY claim in the file claims weight (core.md §6/W2) — not enforced here because that requirement is conditioned on a sibling table's contents, not on [spec] alone. See x-semantic-only-rules 'axis-required-once-any-claim-weighted'.

external.description: OPTIONAL list of normative references not held in the tree.

items.description: A normative reference not in the tree.

version.description: The spec version the [[claim]] `clause` ids refer to.

commit.description: 40 lowercase hex chars — git-domain identity (SHA-1 over the repository tree). NEVER compared against an M11 hash (design rule 4a).

dirty.description: true = uncommitted changes were present at `commit`.

kind.description: The artifact-class registry (format.md '`[subject].kind`'). SEMANTIC NUANCE: this registry is fail-CLOSED-TO-INDETERMINATE in the live validator — a token outside it is `indeterminate`, not a hard `invalid` — which is SOFTER than a strict JSON Schema `enum` (which rejects any other value outright). A third-party schema-only consumer will therefore reject some manifests the validator itself would only flag indeterminate; see x-semantic-only-rules 'subject-kind-registry-fail-closed'.

record_root.description: OPTIONAL. The base path every `record` pointer on this manifest resolves against, instead of the manifest file's own directory (audit F-3).

repo.description: OPTIONAL. An identifier for the subject's own repository; not validator-interpreted.

subject_hash.description: OPTIONAL. The M11 content-hash of the subject artifact, `subject:` domain (design rule 4a). SEMANTIC: when present, every [[claim.evidence]] record naming its own `subject_hash` must equal this value exactly — an equality binding, not a shape constraint.

title: acceptance/0 manifest 0.1.0-draft

x-semantic-only-rules.description: [spec].axis is REQUIRED (nonempty) once ANY [[claim]] in the file claims weight (core.md §6/W2.4); optional in a wholly unweighted manifest.

Oracle-bearing bands (A2/A3/A4, and functional A1) require >=1 observed-red control whose kind is on that band's whitelist and whose carrier record's family is species-compatible with the band (assurance-bands.md rule 6); a 'planted-twin' control never satisfies this gate at any band.
A claim's asserted `band` must be reachable by at least one of its own PASSING evidence records' kind/family (assurance-bands.md rule 2).
status == 'blocked' requires a nonempty blocked_by (core.md §7.3, P4) — an escalation is only greppable if it names what blocks it.

The claim-level `bounds` field, required on grades ['contract', 'probe'], must carry a free-text tail naming the actual limit after the bounded/unbounded token — the token alone is refused (core.md §5).
[[claim]].id must be unique within the file (format.md design rule 6).

[[claim.assumes]] and the Reserved-hooks slots (H1-H8; spec/format.md 'Reserved hooks') are parseable TOML but are read by NO validator function in this revision — neither validated nor rejected. This schema asserts nothing about their shape, on purpose: doing so would not be generated from live registry data, it would be hand-copied prose, exactly the drift risk this whole artifact exists to avoid.
[coverage].claims_total must equal the number of [[claim]] entries actually present.

clause_source is REQUIRED on a weighted claim (core.md W2.3); absent, it is refused into `weight-pending` (an error only under --strict-weight), per the §8.1 transition ratchet, not an unconditional hard error.
clause_source in ['none', 'test-name'] is reserved to mean unweightable by design — a clause read off its own evidence, or off nothing, cannot be falsified (core.md W2).

grade == 'contract' requires >=1 PASSING evidence record whose family is in ['bmc', 'kernel', 'smt-refinement'] (core.md §0.5) — evidence that only enumerates values witnesses points, not sets, and a test is never `contract`.
control.of_claim must equal the id of the [[claim]] the evidence record is nested under; a value naming no claim anywhere in the file is a separate additional error (assurance-bands.md rule 6).

F4: a record may not simultaneously have control.kind == 'mutation', control.observed == 'red', and its own `result` == 'pass' — an observed-red mutation control describes the mutant run, not the baseline run `result` describes.
[coverage].denominator == 'slice' requires a nonempty slice_note (CLAIM-CLASSES-AWAITING-WEIGHT.md C1).

grade == 'contract' additionally requires >=1 PASSING evidence record with epistemic_tier in {T1, T2} (core.md §2, CS-4); transitional, refused into `weight-pending` rather than an unconditional hard error.
A weighted claim requires `grade`; an unweighted claim may omit it entirely (core.md W2). A grade with no deciding machinery is never weight-eligible even when present.
An evidence record's `family` must equal KIND_REGISTRY[kind]['family'] — the registry's own kind-to-family pinning, not independently derivable from `family`'s enum membership alone.
A claim's id/statement SHOULD name the same thing a reader would derive from its evidence's `ref` (format.md design rule 4b) — explicitly NOT mechanically checkable, reviewer work only.

Where `method` names a token the shipped FV profile knows, the profile-pinned tier is a CEILING on `epistemic_tier`: a STRONGER declared tier is an error, a weaker-or-equal one is accepted (evidence-types.md CS-3, ADR-002). An unprofiled `method` makes the record's epistemic_tier `indeterminate`, not a hard error.
mutants_caught >= 1 is additionally required whenever the SAME record's `result` == 'pass' (assurance-bands.md rule 6) — a cross-field floor beyond mutants_caught's own >= 0 type constraint.
status == 'parked' requires a nonempty parked_reason.

Each evidence `kind` in KIND_REGISTRY additionally REQUIRES its own 'extra' fields, at their own per-kind type tag (e.g. kani-harness requires `bounds`+`semantics`; lean-theorem requires `axioms`+`semantics`, `semantics` there being str-nonempty where kani-harness's is str-any). This schema documents the UNION of possible extra fields at their loosest common shape (see each field's own description); the per-kind conditional requiredness and exact tag are not expressed structurally.
self_verify.positive_control must be a PHRASE (>=2 word tokens), not a single token (core.md §4) — the same shape floor as watched_fail.perturbed/observed.

item_kind == 'predicate' requires nonempty `over` and a `covered` fraction N/M with N <= M (core.md §7.2, P3); a weighted predicate row missing either is refused weight outright, an unweighted one only warned.

record_hash is REQUIRED on a weighted, non-illustrative claim's evidence (evidence-types.md P9); when present, the validator recomputes the M11 hash of the `record` file's actual bytes and a mismatch is always an error.

[[claim.evidence]].record must resolve to an existing file (under [subject].record_root, when set) — enforced as an error only under --strict; a warning otherwise. A filesystem check, never expressible in a schema.
Any of ('alpha', 'beta', 'lr') present on an evidence record requires a nonempty `calibration` companion (format.md design rule 3) — trust numbers without calibration are banned.
is_scope_locator checks that scope_ref LOOKS like a locator; that the cited location actually says the item is out of scope is reviewer work, not checkable (core.md §7.1).

[format].shape == 'bundle' makes the validator return `indeterminate` for the WHOLE file, unconditionally, until bundle validation ships (format.md '`shape`') — not a constraint on the `shape` field's own value space.
status in {evidenced, partial} requires >=1 [[claim.evidence]] entry; status in {gap, parked, blocked} requires exactly zero (design rule 1 / core.md §7.3).

status × grade must cohere (core.md §7.1) — a gap/parked/blocked status may not carry a grade asserting a check succeeded, and evidenced/partial may not carry not-covered or out-of-scope. Error on a weighted claim, warning otherwise.
An evidence record's subject_hash, where present, must equal [subject].subject_hash exactly (design rule 4a) — a present-but-unequal pair is a hard error, unconditionally.

[subject].kind outside the shipped registry is `indeterminate`, never a hard `invalid` (format.md '[subject].kind') — SOFTER than this schema's own `enum`, which a strict third-party JSON Schema validator would reject outright. Known, accepted divergence: this schema documents the registry as closed for readability; only check_acceptance.py implements the fail-open-to-indeterminate behaviour.
watched_fail.of_command must equal this claim's own self_verify.command, whitespace-normalized (core.md §4.1) — a control over a different check witnesses nothing about this one.

A weighted claim whose grade is one of ['contract', 'mechanical', 'not-covered', 'probe', 'test-only'] requires a watched-fail witness: a well-formed [claim.self_verify.watched_fail] table, OR an observed-red control naming this claim, OR (grade == 'not-covered' only) a nonempty positive_control (core.md §4.1, W2.5).
